hindi: हे वृत्र का वध करने वाले, रथ पर चढ़ो; तुम्हारे दोनों हरित घोड़े पवित्र वचन से जोते गए हैं। सोम कूटने का पत्थर अपनी ध्वनि से तुम्हारे मन को भली प्रकार हमारी ओर करे। तू उपयाम से ग्रहण किया गया है; तुझे इन्द्र के लिए, षोडशी के लिए। यह तेरा स्थान है; तुझे इन्द्र के लिए, षोडशी के लिए।
english: Mount the chariot, O slayer of Vṛtra; your two bay horses are yoked by the sacred utterance (brahman). May the pressing stone, with its sound, turn your mind well toward us. You are taken with the upayāma; you for Indra, the Ṣoḍaśin. This is your seat; you for Indra, the Ṣoḍaśin.
notes: Line 1 is a Ṛgvedic-type verse; line 2 is the formula of the Ṣoḍaśin cup, with no verb for 'you for Indra' (nothing supplied). 'upayāma-gṛhīta' rendered literally; upayāma is left untranslated. hari = bay horses; the line itself says only 'two bays'. vagnu = sound/call (possibly 'cry'). The final -a of ṣoḍaśina before eṣa is the pausal Vedic sandhi of ṣoḍaśine.

hindi: अपने लम्बे केशों वाले, कक्ष्या भरने वाले बलवान दोनों हरित घोड़ों को जोतो। फिर, हे सोम पीने वाले इन्द्र, हमारे गीतों के श्रवण को प्राप्त हो। तू उपयाम से ग्रहण किया गया है; तुझे इन्द्र के लिए, षोडशी के लिए। यह तेरा स्थान है; तुझे इन्द्र के लिए, षोडशी के लिए।
english: Yoke the two long-maned bay stallions, who fill the girth. Then, O Indra, drinker of Soma, come to hear our songs. You are taken with the upayāma; you for Indra, the Ṣoḍaśin. This is your seat; you for Indra, the Ṣoḍaśin.
notes: 'upaśrutim cara' rendered 'come to hear'; 'kakṣya-prā' (filling the girth) is obscure and rendered literally. 'naḥ' taken as 'our' with girām (could also be 'for us'). Token 'girāmupaśrutim' is a single token, so the split shows girām + upa-śrutim in one token.

hindi: दोनों हरित घोड़े अजेय बल वाले इन्द्र को ही ऋषियों की स्तुतियों और मनुष्यों के यज्ञ के पास ले जाते हैं। तू उपयाम से ग्रहण किया गया है; तुझे इन्द्र के लिए, षोडशी के लिए। यह तेरा स्थान है; तुझे इन्द्र के लिए, षोडशी के लिए।
english: The two bay horses carry Indra, of unassailed strength, to the praises of the sages and to the sacrifice of men. You are taken with the upayāma; you for Indra, the Ṣoḍaśin. This is your seat; you for Indra, the Ṣoḍaśin.

text_flags.why: possible: avagraha missing before sīndrāya (asi + indrāya); the Devanagari also lacks it

notes: Line 2: 'gṛhīto sīndrāya' appears as two tokens with no avagraha. In line 1, 'iddharī' = it + harī; the verb vahataḥ is dual to match the two horses.

words.gram: pres. part. mid. m. nom. sg. sam-√rā

hindi: जिससे बढ़कर कोई दूसरा उत्पन्न नहीं हुआ है, जो सब लोकों में प्रविष्ट हुआ है, वह प्रजापति प्रजा के साथ आनन्दित होता हुआ तीन ज्योतियों का सेवन करता है; वही षोडशी है।
english: Than whom no other, higher one has been born, who has entered all the worlds: that Prajāpati, delighting with offspring, attends the three lights; he is the Ṣoḍaśin.
notes: 'yasmān na jātaḥ paro anyaḥ asti' is literally 'from whom no other beyond is born'; the order of the relative clauses is kept as in the verse. 'saṃrarāṇaḥ' (from sam-√rā) is rendered 'delighting', but 'bestowing' is possible; 'sacate' = attends/follows (could also be 'is joined to'). The three 'lights' are not named in the line.

words.gram: pres. part. mid. f. nom. sg. √juṣ

hindi: इन्द्र और सम्राट् वरुण राजा, उन दोनों ने पहले तुम्हारे लिए यह भक्ष बनाया। उन दोनों के पीछे मैं भक्ष का भक्षण करता हूँ; वाग्देवी सेवन करती हुई सोम से तृप्त हो, प्राण के साथ। स्वाहा।
english: Indra, and Varuṇa the supreme ruler and king: those two made this portion for you at first. After those two I partake of the portion; may the goddess Speech, enjoying it, be satisfied with the Soma, together with the breath. Svāhā.
notes: 'samrāj' may qualify Indra ('Indra the supreme ruler and Varuṇa the king') or Varuṇa; the word order is ambiguous. 'te' addressed to the Soma/portion (not stated who). 'agre' rendered 'at first/in front'.

hindi: हे अग्नि, तू शुद्ध हो, सुकर्म वाले; हमारे लिए तेज और उत्तम वीर्य, और मुझमें धन और पुष्टि को स्थापित करता हुआ। तू उपयाम से ग्रहण किया गया है; तुझे अग्नि के लिए, तेज के लिए। यह तेरा स्थान है; तुझे अग्नि के लिए, तेज के लिए। हे अग्नि, तेजस्वी, तू देवों में तेजस्वी है; मैं मनुष्यों में तेजस्वी होऊँ।
english: O Agni, purify yourself, skilful in work: for us splendour and good heroic strength, placing wealth and nourishment in me. You are taken with the upayāma; you for Agni, for splendour. This is your seat; you for Agni, for splendour. O Agni, splendid one, you are splendid among the gods; may I be splendid among men.
notes: Line 1 has no finite verb besides pavasva; 'varcaḥ suvīryam' are accusatives and are rendered as the things sought, with dadhat 'placing' (the verse does not say what is placed for us). 'svapāḥ' = 'skilful in work' (apas = work). 'varca̭sa' at the end of the second line is the pausal form of varcase.

words.gram: pres. part. m. nom. sg. ud-√sthā

hindi: उठते हुए, बल के साथ, चमसों में निचोड़े गए सोम को पीकर, हे इन्द्र, तूने दोनों जबड़ों को हिला दिया। तू उपयाम से ग्रहण किया गया है; तुझे इन्द्र के लिए, बल के लिए। यह तेरा स्थान है; तुझे इन्द्र के लिए, बल के लिए। हे इन्द्र, अत्यन्त बलवान, तू देवों में अत्यन्त बलवान है; मैं मनुष्यों में अत्यन्त बलवान होऊँ।
english: Rising up with strength, having drunk the Soma pressed in the two cups, O Indra, you made your two jaws shake. You are taken with the upayāma; you for Indra, for strength. This is your seat; you for Indra, for strength. O Indra, mightiest one, you are mightiest among the gods; may I be mightiest among men.
notes: 'camū' is taken as a dual locative 'in the two cups' (possible alternatives: 'in the cup'); 'śipre' = jaws (or lips/nose-guards), sense uncertain; 'avepayaḥ' is the causative 'made shake'. 'tvauja̭sa' = tvā + ojase.

hindi: उसके केतु दिखाई दिए, उसकी किरणें लोगों पर फैलकर, अग्नियों के समान चमकती हुई। तू उपयाम से ग्रहण किया गया है; तुझे सूर्य के लिए, दीप्ति के लिए। यह तेरा स्थान है; तुझे सूर्य के लिए, दीप्ति के लिए। हे सूर्य, अत्यन्त दीप्तिमान, तू देवों में अत्यन्त दीप्तिमान है; मैं मनुष्यों में अत्यन्त दीप्तिमान होऊँ।
english: His banners have been seen, his rays widely over the people, shining like fires. You are taken with the upayāma; you for Sūrya, for radiance. This is your seat; you for Sūrya, for radiance. O Sūrya, most radiant one, you are most radiant among the gods; may I be most radiant among men.
notes: 'ketu' rendered 'banner, sign' (could be 'ray' or 'brightness'); 'vi' read with adṛśram ('widely'). 'janā~2' is the printed form of janān with a prolonged vowel mark. 'bhrājāyaiṣa' = bhrājāya + eṣaḥ.

hindi: उस जातवेदस देव को, सूर्य को, केतु ऊपर ले जाते हैं, सबके दर्शन के लिए। तू उपयाम से ग्रहण किया गया है; तुझे सूर्य के लिए, दीप्ति के लिए। यह तेरा स्थान है; तुझे सूर्य के लिए, दीप्ति के लिए।
english: The banners carry up that god Jātavedas, Sūrya, to be seen by all. You are taken with the upayāma; you for Sūrya, for radiance. This is your seat; you for Sūrya, for radiance.
notes: 'ketavaḥ' rendered 'banners'; 'viśvāya' with 'dṛśe' as 'for all to see'. 'Jātavedas' is kept as a name; the line sets it beside 'devam sūryam' without further identification.

hindi: कलश को सूँघ, हे महान; ये बूँदें तुझमें प्रवेश करें। फिर ऊर्जा के साथ लौट आ; वह तू विशाल धाराओं वाली और दूध से भरी हुई हमारे लिए हजार दुह। फिर मुझमें धन प्रवेश करे।
english: Smell the vessel, O great one; may the drops enter you. Turn back again with vigour; you, of wide streams and rich in milk, yield us a thousand. May wealth enter me again.
notes: 'mahi' is uncertain (vocative 'great one' or adverbial 'greatly'); the addressee, feminine in line 2, is not named. 'ūrjā' = with vigour (or 'sap, nourishment'). 'sahasram' has no stated noun ('a thousand'). 'viśatāt' read as 3 sg. imv. in -tāt, 'may wealth enter me'.

hindi: हे इडा, रन्ता, हव्या, काम्या, चन्द्रा, ज्योता, अदिति, सरस्वती, महि, विश्रुति; हे अघ्न्या, ये तेरे नाम हैं। देवों के लिए मुझे सुकर्म करने वाला कह।
english: O Iḍā, Rantā, Havyā, Kāmyā, Candrā, Jyotā, Aditi, Sarasvatī, Mahī, Viśruti: these are your names, O inviolable one. Declare me to the gods as one who does well.
notes: The ten vocatives are read as names or titles (the line does not say whose); 'jyote' (jyotā) and 'rante', 'havye' are uncertain forms. 'aghnyā' = 'not to be killed' (inviolable); the line states no identity. 'brūtāt' read as 2 sg. imperative 'declare' (3 sg. 'let him declare' is grammatically possible); 'mā sukṛtam' = 'me as a doer of good'.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, हमारे शत्रुओं को दूर कर दे; आक्रमण करने वालों को नीचा कर। जो हमारे प्रति शत्रुता करता है, उसे नीचे के अन्धकार में पहुँचा। तू उपयाम से ग्रहण किया गया है; तुझे इन्द्र के लिए, विमृध के लिए। यह तेरा स्थान है; तुझे इन्द्र के लिए, विमृध के लिए।
english: O Indra, strike our foes apart; hold down those who offer us battle. Whoever acts hostilely toward us, make him go to the lower darkness. You are taken with the upayāma; you for Indra, for Vimṛdh (the foe-repeller). This is your seat; you for Indra, for Vimṛdh (the foe-repeller).
notes: 'vimṛdh' (dative vimṛdhe) is kept as a name-like epithet, glossed literally 'foe-repeller'. 'abhidāsati' (denominative from dāsa) is rendered 'acts hostilely'. The object of 'gamaya' ('him') is not stated. 'a̱smā~2' is asmān with a prolonged vowel mark.

hindi: वाचस्पति, विश्वकर्मा को, जो मन के समान वेग वाले हैं, सहायता के लिए आज बल के लिए हम बुलाएँ। वह सर्वकल्याणकारी, सुकर्म वाला, हमारे सब आह्वानों को सहायता के लिए स्वीकार करे। तू उपयाम से ग्रहण किया गया है; तुझे इन्द्र के लिए, विश्वकर्मा के लिए। यह तेरा स्थान है; तुझे इन्द्र के लिए, विश्वकर्मा के लिए।
english: Vācaspati, Viśvakarman, swift as thought, we call today for help, for strength. May he, all-beneficent and of good work, accept all our invocations for help. You are taken with the upayāma; you for Indra, for Viśvakarman. This is your seat; you for Indra, for Viśvakarman.
notes: 'vācaspatim viśvakarmāṇam' are taken as two names of one being (the line does not say so); 'vāje' (loc.) rendered 'for strength' (or 'in the contest'); 'joṣat' read as 3 sg. subjunctive used as imperative. The formula lines read 'indrāya tvā viśvakarmaṇe' with no linking word between the two datives.

hindi: हे विश्वकर्मा, बढ़ाने वाली हवि से तूने इन्द्र को रक्षक और अवध्य बनाया। उसके सामने बहुत सी प्रजाएँ झुक गईं, जिससे यह उग्र और आह्वान के योग्य हो। तू उपयाम से ग्रहण किया गया है; तुझे इन्द्र के लिए, विश्वकर्मा के लिए। यह तेरा स्थान है; तुझे इन्द्र के लिए, विश्वकर्मा के लिए।
english: O Viśvakarman, with the strengthening offering you made Indra a protector, unslayable. To him the many peoples bowed together, so that this one might be mighty and to be invoked in contest. You are taken with the upayāma; you for Indra, for Viśvakarman. This is your seat; you for Indra, for Viśvakarman.
notes: 'pūrvīḥ' agrees with viśaḥ and is rendered 'many' (or 'former'); 'vihavya' = 'to be invoked in contest' (or 'to be called upon variously'). Line 3 prints 'viśvakarmaṇa' (final -a) before the next line's 'eṣa': this is the pausal sandhi (e + e) of the edition, so the word is read viśvakarmaṇe, and no change is proposed.

hindi: तू उपयाम से ग्रहण किया गया है; तुझे अग्नि के लिए गायत्र छन्द वाले को मैं ग्रहण करता हूँ; तुझे इन्द्र के लिए त्रिष्टुप् छन्द वाले को मैं ग्रहण करता हूँ; तुझे सब देवों के लिए जगती छन्द वाले को मैं ग्रहण करता हूँ; अनुष्टुप् तेरा अभिगर है।
english: You are taken with the upayāma; you for Agni, of the Gāyatra metre, I take; you for Indra, of the Triṣṭubh metre, I take; you for all the gods, of the Jagatī metre, I take; the Anuṣṭubh is your abhigara.
notes: 'abhigara' is kept untranslated in Hindi and glossed 'acclamation' in the word list (the exact sense, such as 'responsive call' or 'accompaniment', is uncertain). 'chandas' is read as the metre of the verse accompanying the taking; the line states no more.

hindi: व्रेशियों की उड़ान में तुझे हिलाता हूँ; कुकूननाओं की उड़ान में तुझे हिलाता हूँ; आनन्द मनाने वालियों की उड़ान में तुझे हिलाता हूँ; अत्यन्त मद देने वालियों की उड़ान में तुझे हिलाता हूँ; अत्यन्त मधुर वालियों की उड़ान में तुझे हिलाता हूँ। उज्ज्वल तुझे उज्ज्वल में हिलाता हूँ, दिन के रूप में, सूर्य की किरणों में।
english: I shake you in the flight of the Vreśīs; I shake you in the flight of the Kukūnanas; I shake you in the flight of the exulting ones; I shake you in the flight of the most intoxicating ones; I shake you in the flight of the sweetest ones. I shake you, the bright one, in the bright; in the form of the day, in the rays of Sūrya.
notes: 'vreśīnām' and 'kukūnanānām' are obscure and kept as transliterated names; the line does not say what the genitive plurals refer to (feminine plural assumed from the endings). 'patman' (loc.) rendered 'in the flight' (or 'in the fall, course'). 'tvā patmann ā dhūnomi' repeated for each genitive. 'madintamānām' and 'madhuntamānām' are superlatives with the nasal inserted before -tama.

hindi: बैल का ऊँचा रूप चमकता है; बृहत् शुक्र शुक्र का अग्रगामी है, सोम सोम का अग्रगामी है। हे सोम, तेरा जो न ठगा जाने वाला, जागता हुआ नाम है, उसके लिए तुझे ग्रहण करता हूँ; उसके लिए, हे सोम, तेरे लिए, सोम के लिए, स्वाहा।
english: The lofty form of the bull shines; the great bright one is the leader of the bright one, Soma is the leader of Soma. That name of yours, O Soma, the unbeguilable, the wakeful: for that I take you; for that, for you, O Soma, for Soma: svāhā.
notes: 'kakubha' is read as 'lofty' (kakubh = peak; the form may also be a name); 'bṛhacchukraḥ' is read as 'bṛhat' + 'śukraḥ' (a compound 'bṛhat-śukra' is also possible). In line 2 the repeated 'tasmai' leaves 'for that (name)' unspoken. 'te' and 'tvā' both address Soma.

hindi: उत्सुक तू, हे देव सोम, अग्नि के प्रिय पाथ में जा। इच्छुक तू, हे देव सोम, इन्द्र के प्रिय पाथ में जा। हमारा मित्र तू, हे देव सोम, सब देवों के प्रिय पाथ में जा।
english: Eager, you, O god Soma, go into the dear pāthas of Agni. Willing, you, O god Soma, go into the dear pāthas of Indra. Our friend, you, O god Soma, go into the dear pāthas of all the gods.
notes: 'pāthas' is left untranslated: it can mean 'drink' or 'place, abode'. 'uśik' and 'vaśī' (both from vaś 'to wish') are rendered 'eager, willing'. Printed 'apīhi' is read api + ihi (go into). In line 2 the token 'pātho'pīhyasmatsakhā' ends one clause (pāthaḥ api ihi) and begins the next (asmat-sakhā).

words.gram: pres. part. m. nom. sg. upa-√sṛj

hindi: यहाँ रति है; यहाँ आनन्द करो; यहाँ धृति है; यहाँ स्वधृति है। स्वाहा। माता को आधार भेजता हुआ, आधार देने वाला माता को पीता हुआ, हमारे बीच धन की वृद्धि को धारण करे। स्वाहा।
english: Here is delight; here take delight; here is steadiness; here is self-support. Svāhā. Sending forth a support to the mother, the supporter sucking the mother: may he hold increase of wealth in us. Svāhā.
notes: 'dharuṇa' is rendered 'support' (it may also mean a sustaining fluid); 'dhayan' = 'sucking'; the subject of 'dīdharat' is the supporter. 'ramadhvam' is plural (addressed to several).

hindi: तू यज्ञसत्र की समृद्धि है। हम ज्योति को प्राप्त हुए हैं, हम अमर हो गए हैं। हम पृथ्वी से स्वर्ग पर चढ़े हैं, हमने देवों को और स्वर्ग की ज्योति को पाया है।
english: You are the prosperity of the sacrificial session. We have gone to the light; we have become immortal. We have climbed from the earth to heaven; we have found the gods and the heavenly light.
notes: 'pṛthivyā' is read as the ablative 'pṛthivyāḥ' (with adhi, 'from the earth'). 'adhyā'ruhāma' is read adhi + āruhāma (the apostrophe mark is part of the edition's token). 'divam' could also be 'sky'.

hindi: हे इन्द्र और पर्वत, आगे लड़ने वाले तुम दोनों, जो हमसे लड़े, उसे दूर मारो; वज्र से उसे ही मारो, उसे ही मारो। दूर, छिपाए हुए के लिए, वह घना स्थान ढक दे जिसमें वह पहुँचे। हे शूर, हमारे शत्रुओं को चारों ओर से तोड़ने वाला तोड़ डाले, सब ओर से। भूः भुवः स्वः। हम प्रजाओं से उत्तम प्रजा वाले, वीरों से उत्तम वीरों वाले, पोषणों से उत्तम पोषण वाले हों।
english: You two, O Indra and Parvata, fighters in front: whoever would fight against us, strike him away; with the thunderbolt strike him, him indeed. Far away, for the concealed one, may it conceal the thicket which he reaches. O hero, may the shatterer shatter our enemies all around, on all sides. Bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ. May we be rich in offspring through offspring, rich in heroes through heroes, rich in nourishment through nourishments.
notes: Line 2 is obscure: 'cattāya' (perhaps 'concealed, hidden') and 'chantsat' (desiderative of √chad, 'may it wish to cover') are uncertain, so the rendering is tentative and no firm reading is built on it. In line 3 'darmā' is read as a noun 'shatterer' (subject of darṣīṣṭa). In line 1 'tam id hatam' is repeated for emphasis. 'bhūrbhuvaḥ' is kept as the two utterances bhūḥ and bhuvaḥ.

words.gloss: Parameṣṭhin, one in the highest place

hindi: परमेष्ठी अभिधीत; प्रजापति वाणी में उच्चारित होने पर; अन्धस् समीप गया हुआ। सविता सन्या में; विश्वकर्मा दीक्षा में; पूषा सोमक्रयणी में।
english: Parameṣṭhin, enclosed (abhidhīta); Prajāpati, in speech when uttered; the andhas, gone toward. Savitṛ in the sanyā; Viśvakarman in the consecration; Pūṣan in the Soma-purchase.
notes: The unit is a list of paired names and states with no verbs. 'abhidhītaḥ', 'andhas', 'acchetaḥ' (read acchā + itaḥ), 'sanyā' and 'somakrayaṇī' are uncertain and rendered literally or left in Sanskrit; the line does not say what the names stand for, so none is added.

words.gram: pres. part. pass. m. nom. sg. √paṇ

hindi: इन्द्र और मरुत् क्रय के लिए उठे हुए; असुर मोल-भाव किया जाता हुआ; मित्र खरीदा हुआ; विष्णु शिपिविष्ट चौड़े स्थान पर बैठा हुआ; विष्णु नरन्धिष।
english: Indra and the Maruts, risen up for the purchase; the asura, being bargained for; Mitra, bought; Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa, seated on the broad (place); Viṣṇu Narandhiṣa.
notes: GROUPING: the list pairs a name with a state participle; the next unit's first word 'prohyamāṇaḥ' (being carried forward) probably belongs here after 'viṣṇur narandhiṣaḥ' (the unit division of the edition is kept). 'upotthitaḥ' is singular after two subjects. 'urāvāsannaḥ' is read urau + āsannaḥ ('seated on the broad place'); 'uru-āsanna' is possible. 'śipiviṣṭa' and 'narandhiṣa' are epithets of unclear sense.

words.gram: pres. part. pass. m. nom. sg. pra-√vah
pres. part. pass. m. nom. sg. upa-ava-√hṛ

hindi: आगे ले जाया जाता हुआ; सोम आया हुआ; वरुण आसन्दी पर बैठा हुआ; अग्नि आग्नीध्र में; इन्द्र हविर्धान में; अथर्वा नीचे लाया जाता हुआ।
english: Being carried forward; Soma, come; Varuṇa, seated on the seat (āsandī); Agni in the Āgnīdhra; Indra in the havirdhāna; Atharvan, being carried down toward.
notes: GROUPING: 'prohyamāṇaḥ' probably goes with the end of unit 55 ('viṣṇuḥ narandhiṣaḥ prohyamāṇaḥ'), since the list pairs a name with a participle; the edition's division is kept here. 'āgnīdhra' is printed with final -a (pausal e before indro), read āgnīdhre (locative; Āgnīdhra is the priest or his place, not decided). 'atharvā' (from 'tharvā after avagraha) is uncertain.

words.gram: pres. part. pass. m. nom. sg. ā-√pyāy
pres. part. pass. m. nom. sg. √su

words.gloss: (end of sūyamānaḥ, split by a stray space)

words.gram: pres. part. pass. m. nom. sg. sam-√bhṛ
pres. part. pass. m. nom. sg. √pū

hindi: सब देव अंशुओं में रखे हुए; विष्णु आप्रीतपा बढ़ाया जाता हुआ; यम निचोड़ा जाता हुआ; विष्णु इकट्ठा किया जाता हुआ; वायु शुद्ध किया जाता हुआ; शुक्र शुद्ध किया हुआ; शुक्र दूध से मिला हुआ; मन्थी; सत्तू से मिला हुआ।
english: All the gods, deposited in the aṃśus; Viṣṇu, āprītapā, being swollen; Yama, being pressed; Viṣṇu, being gathered; Vāyu, being purified; Śukra, purified; Śukra, mixed with milk; the manthin; mixed with barley meal.

text_flags.why: possible: stray space inside sūyamānaḥ (yamaḥ sūyamānaḥ); the Devanagari has the same split

notes: List of names each paired with a state participle, with no verbs; the line does not say what the names stand for. 'āprītapā' is obscure (kept as a transliteration). 'kṣīra-śrīḥ' and 'saktu-śrīḥ' read as 'mixed with milk / with barley meal' (√śrī); 'manthī' read as 'manthin', a mixed drink or its name. 'aṃśu' is left untranslated.

words.gram: pres. part. pass. m. nom. sg. √hu
pres. part. pass. m. nom. sg. √bhakṣ

hindi: सब देव चमसों में ऊपर उठाए हुए; असु होम के लिए उठाया हुआ; रुद्र आहुति दिया जाता हुआ; वात लौटा हुआ; नृचक्षा प्रख्यात। भक्ष भक्षण किया जाता हुआ; पितर नाराशंस।
english: All the gods, taken up in the cups; the life-breath, lifted up for the oblation; Rudra, being offered; Vāta, turned toward; Nṛcakṣas, regarded; the portion, being partaken; the Fathers, the Nārāśaṃsas.
notes: List of names paired with participles, no verbs. 'asuḥ' read as life-breath (not 'asura'); 'nṛcakṣāḥ' kept as a name with a literal gloss; 'nārāśaṃsāḥ' kept in Sanskrit. 'pratikhyātaḥ' rendered 'regarded' (or 'named'). The sense of the pairs is not given by the line.

words.gram: pres. part. pass. m. nom. sg. abhi-ava-√hṛ

hindi: बैठा हुआ; सिन्धु अवभृथ के लिए उठाया हुआ; समुद्र नीचे ले जाया जाता हुआ; सलिल बहता हुआ। जिन दोनों के बल से लोक थामे गए, जो अपने वीर कर्मों से अत्यन्त वीर और सबसे बलवान हैं; जो दोनों अपने बलों से अप्रतिहत होकर स्वामित्व करते हैं, वे विष्णु और वरुण पहली पुकार पर आए।
english: Settled; the river, lifted up for the avabhṛtha; the sea, being carried down; the water, flooding forth. They two by whose strength the airy realms were propped, most heroic by their heroic deeds, the strongest; they two who rule unopposed with their powers, Viṣṇu and Varuṇa, came at the first invocation.
notes: GROUPING: 'sannaḥ' (first word) probably belongs with the end of unit 58 ('pitaro nārāśaṃsāḥ sannaḥ'), since the list pairs names with participles; the edition's division is kept. Lines 2 and 3 are a verse; 'viṣṇū' and 'varuṇā' are dual-looking forms read as 'Viṣṇu and Varuṇa' (the two named as a pair is uncertain). 'agan' (3 pl.) is used of the two. 'rajāṃsi' rendered 'airy realms' (or 'worlds').

hindi: यज्ञ देवों के पास, स्वर्ग को गया है; उससे मुझे धन प्राप्त हो। यज्ञ मनुष्यों के पास, अन्तरिक्ष को गया है; उससे मुझे धन प्राप्त हो। यज्ञ पितरों के पास, पृथ्वी को गया है; उससे मुझे धन प्राप्त हो। यज्ञ जिस किसी लोक को गया है, उससे मेरा कल्याण हुआ है।
english: The sacrifice has gone to the gods, to heaven; from that may wealth reach me. The sacrifice has gone to men, to the atmosphere; from that may wealth reach me. The sacrifice has gone to the Fathers, to the earth; from that may wealth reach me. To whatever world the sacrifice has gone, from that good has come to me.
notes: 'devān divam agan yajñaḥ' read as 'the sacrifice has gone to the gods, to heaven' (the pairing of each group with its realm is the line's own). 'aṣṭu' from √aś (reach). 'bhadraṃma̭bhūt' = bhadram + abhūt.

hindi: जो चौंतीस तन्तु फैलाए गए हैं, जो इस यज्ञ को स्वधा के साथ देते हैं, उनका जो कटा हुआ है, उसे मैं जोड़कर रखता हूँ। स्वाहा। घर्म देवों के पास जाए।
english: The thirty-four threads that have been stretched out, which give this sacrifice with svadhā: what is severed of them I put together. Svāhā. May the hot offering go to the gods.
notes: 'samvetaddadhāmi' is read sam + u + etat + dadhāmi (the u becoming v before a vowel); 'sam etat' with a different second element is possible, so this is tentative. 'dadante' (give) takes the sacrifice as object; the threads are not identified. 'chinna' = severed.

words.gloss: (end of prajāyām, split by a stray space)

hindi: यज्ञ का दोह अनेक स्थानों में फैला हुआ है; उसने आठ प्रकार से स्वर्ग के साथ-साथ विस्तार किया। हे यज्ञ, वह तू मेरे लिए प्रजा में, बहुत धन की पुष्टि दुह; मैं पूर्ण आयु प्राप्त करूँ। स्वाहा।
english: The yield of the sacrifice is spread out in many places; he stretched eightfold along heaven. That you, O sacrifice, yield greatly for me in offspring an increase of wealth; may I attain the full life. Svāhā.

text_flags.why: possible: stray space inside prajāyām (loc. sg.), before rāyaspoṣam; the Devanagari has the same split

notes: 'saḥ' in line 1 is 'he' (the sacrifice or its yield; not stated). 'mahi' may be 'greatly' or an adjective with the yield; 'prajāyām' read as locative 'in offspring' (the stray space splits the word).

hindi: हे सोम, सोने से युक्त, घोड़ों से युक्त और वीरों से युक्त होकर बह; गायों से युक्त बल ले आ। स्वाहा।
english: Flow clear hither, O Soma, with gold, with horses, with heroes; bring strength rich in cattle. Svāhā.
notes: 'pavasva' (√pū) is rendered 'flow clear'; 'hiraṇya-vat' etc. are adverbial '-vat' forms ('endowed with'). The line has the first half-verse and the second half-verse, ending with svāhā.
